validity.recommendation: Check length and diameter against a Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine technical document. Three sources give three lengths. The start year looks like 1961, not 1960.
validity.researcher_notes: Existence is solid. The line is named by a 2011 Ukrainian news report, by a design institute table of Soviet trunk lines (archived 2022), by Ukrainian Wikipedia and by the Ukrtransgaz company timeline (1961). It is a transmission trunk, not a feeder, and it is not a duplicate of its two sister lines. The design institute table lists three separate lines in one block, Shebelinka-Poltava-Kyiv at 700 mm and 438 km, Efremovka-Dikanka-Kyiv at 1000 mm and 477.8 km, and Shebelinka-Dikanka-Kyiv at 1000 mm and 522 km. The names in the block map in order onto the data rows. Length conflict: the sheet says 454.7 km, the design table says 438 km, and Ukrainian Wikipedia says 478 km. Diameter: 720 mm in the 2011 news report, 700 mm elsewhere, probably the nominal and outer sizes of one pipe. Start year: 1961 per Wikipedia and the company timeline against 1960 on the sheet.

fills.researcher_notes: A Ukrainian news report from September 2011 says the Shebelinka-Poltava-Kyiv trunk line was carrying gas at 40 atmospheres when a construction crew damaged it near Boryspil. That shows it was in service in 2011. No source dated 2024 or later was found that names this line. The 2024 Ukrainian Wikipedia article on the corridor describes it as part of the working network but is not a current status source. Tier is medium because the evidence is old.

fills.researcher_notes: Two sources say the line was commissioned in 1961. Ukrainian Wikipedia says it was put into operation in 1961. The Ukrtransgaz company history timeline, read from an archived copy, gives the same year under 1961. The sheet says 1960. A 2011 news article said the line was built in 1960, and that fits first gas flowing in 1960 by a bypass while the line itself was commissioned in 1961. I propose 1961 and keep the old value in this note. Ukrtransgaz and the regional news outlet are separate origins from Wikipedia only in part, so independence is marked as true on the company timeline and Wikipedia pair.

Searched Ukrainian and Russian for a design or current throughput for Shebelinka-Poltava-Kyiv in the design institute table, Ukrainian Wikipedia, the Ukrtransgaz timeline and news. None gives a figure for this line alone. The design institute table lists pressure (5.4 MPa) but not capacity. No capacity was found, so the cell stays blank.

The sheet says 454.7 km. A 2011 Ukrainian news article (jkg-portal.com.ua) states 454.7 km, but that site timed out today and was not re-verified, so it is not restaged. The design institute table (archived 2022) gives 438 km for this line, and Ukrainian Wikipedia gives 478 km. Three sources, three figures. No verified source states 454.7 km, so no ref is proposed. See the length concern in the validity record.

The 2011 news report states 720 mm exactly. The design institute table and Ukrainian Wikipedia both say 700 mm. A 700 mm nominal pipe has a 720 mm outer diameter, so these are likely the same pipe named two ways. The sheet value stays at 720 mm and the 700 mm figure is noted.

fills.researcher_notes: The design institute table lists the line as Shebelinka-Poltava-Kyiv with Ukraine as the only country. The 2011 news report places a rupture on it near Boryspil, on the Kyiv side. Start and end are both in Ukraine.

The Operator cell is blank. The owner is recorded as the Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine, which has run Ukraine's gas trunk lines since 1 January 2020, so it is probably the operator too. No source verified today names this line under that company. The company site returns an access block and its archived copy was unreachable. Left blank rather than guess.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The newest dated evidence naming this line is the September 2011 news report of a rupture while in service. Searches in Ukrainian and Russian for 2024 or later items found nothing that names this line. The gas trunk network is still in domestic use after Russian transit ended on 1 January 2025, but no source says so for this line. No change is proposed and the status is kept as recorded. Absence of news is not evidence of closure.
